newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific flaring ruptured NGL line.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific flaring ruptured NGL line.

text.p: Union Pacific Resources Group on Thursday was flaring natural gas liquids from a ruptured 10-inch pipeline in east Texas that forced the evacuation of a local community, a company spokesman said.

The pipeline, which was ruptured by a construction crew laying a parallel pipe under a creek bed, moves liquids between Carthage, Texas and an Enterprise refinery at Mont Belvieu on the Texas coast, company officials said.
The Fort Worth-based company, which moves ethane, propane and butane on the line, diverted shipments from the 25,000 barrel per day pipeline onto a nearby Chevron pipeline.
"We couldn't make product for eight hours," following the Thursday morning rupture, said Bert Dillmann, Union Pacific Resources operations manager.

Blow-down valves closest to the rupture were being flared to depressurize an eight mile section of the line, and repairs were expected to take about two weeks because the pipe was ruptured about 50 feet below a creek bed, the spokesman said.

Evacuation of nearby Big Thicket, Texas was hampered after heavy rains washed out an earthen dam, stranding some residents, officials said. Residents were being kept away from the area where vapors were dissipating to avoid an explosion.
